channel.title: Africanews RSS
channel.description: Receive free and in real-time all news published by africanews.com, by subscribing to our RSS feeds.

item.title: Brazil's Lula, Bolsonaro snub final TV debate ahead of Sunday's polls
item.description: Leftist President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro are frontrunners in Sunday's race. Both skipped a planned TV debate, opting to avoid direct confrontation before the first round of voting.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Union of Arab Football Associations backs FIFA chief Infantino
item.description: The Union of Arab Football Associations says it is backing embattled FIFA head Gianni Infantino in his bid for reelection next year.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Burkina Faso deaf dancers use special technique to follow rhythm
item.description: Deaf and hearing impaired people in Burkina Faso are using a special technique to dance. The Vibra-Signe technique helps them feel the rhythm and has opened up new social possibilities for the often marginalised group.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: 'Sad exit': Portugal fans mourn hinted end of Ronaldo era
item.description: Portugal fans are in mourning as Cristiano Ronaldo is seemingly living his last moments with the national team. The star forward walked out of the team’s training camp on Wednesday, hours after coach Jorge Jesus said he would not start Thursday’s Nations League game against Denmark.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: 2025 AFCON final: CAS to hear Senegal appeal on October 8
item.description: The Court of Arbitration for Sport will hear Senegal’s appeal over the disputed 2025 Africa Cup of Nations final against Morocco on October 8 in Lausanne.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Egypt expels Ethiopian diplomat in growing rife over Blue Nile dam
item.description: The tit for tat move on Thursday came after Addis Ababa expelled an Egyptian official, further straining relations between the two countries.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Residents of Kenya's Lamu island fear damage from mega-refinery
item.description: The Kenyan island of Lamu is known for its stunning Indian Ocean setting and 12th-century Old Town. Cars are non-existent here and transport mostly happens by donkey. But the island is about to become home to one of Kenya’s largest industrial projects, raising fears of environmental damage.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Russian president warns Moscow will use ‘all weapons’ to defend Kaliningrad
item.description: Vladimir Putin has accused NATO of preparing to blockade the strategic Russian exclave which lies between two alliance members, Poland and Lithuania.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Pix of the Day, 2 October, 2026 - Across the world
item.description: Pix of the Day, 2 October, 2026 - Across the world
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Mobile labs speed up Ebola testing in eastern DR Congo
item.description: In the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, a mobile lab has been operating for two weeks, a welcome relief to staff at the nearby Ebola treatment centre who said that getting a test result used to take 72 hours.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Tinubu's economic reforms draw mixed reactions ahead of Nigeria election
item.description: Nigeria celebrated 66 years of independence on Thursday, marked by a speech from President Bola Tinubu. Tinubu, who is running for a second term in January, said the country has overcome some major challenges since he took office in 2023, but citizens are skeptical.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Guinea's exiled former PM Sidya Touré to be buried in Ivory Coast
item.description: Sidya Touré died in Paris last week. His family said the former Guinean prime minister will be buried in Ivory Coast.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Carlos Queiroz leaves Ghana job again after just one month
item.description: The Portuguese coach had rejoined the Black Starts his September. His second departure comes after Ghana was beaten by Ivory Coast and by Gambia in qualifying matches for the Africa Cup of Nations last month.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Guinea-Bissau junta blocks Embaló’s planned return, citing security concerns
item.description: Earlier this week, former president Umaro Sissoco Embaló said he would come back to Guinea-Bissau. But on Thursday, the military high command said it refused his return, citing national security, public order and the need to preserve social stability.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Ethiopia and Eritrea sever diplomatic ties as Tigray fighting intensifies
item.description: Addis Ababa accused Eritrea of supporting the Tigray People's Liberation Front, which has launched attacks into the neighbouring Afar and Amhara regions. Ethiopia said it would expel 10 Eritrean diplomats and close its embassy in Asmara.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Egypt arrests entire newsroom of 'unlicensed' independent outlet
item.description: Egypt's interior ministry said Thursday it arrested six staff members of a fact-checking platform it accused of being "unlicensed" and linked to the banned Muslim Brotherhood group.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Former Sudanese president Bashir hospitalized in Khartoum
item.description: Omar al Bashir was being treated at an army hospital in the Sudanese capital Thursday, according to his lawyer. The 82-year-old has spent most of his life, since his ouster in 2019, between hospital and prison.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Libya's pay strike rallies teachers across divided nation
item.description: Classes for some 1.6 million public-school students were due to start in early September but have been postponed indefinitely, as teachers regularly take to the streets to protest over unmet demands.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Mixed reactions after prominent Zimbabwe businessman dies in helicopter crash
item.description: Wicknell Chivayo was one of the most recognisable faces of a class of conspicuously wealthy entrepreneurs with ties to Zimbabwe's ruling party. His death sparked mixed reactions in the country.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com

item.title: G20: Russia criticises US and warns of trade order disintegration
item.description: Speaking during a two-day gathering of G20 trade ministers, Russian Minister of Economic Development Maxim Reshetnikov said the rules of global trade were being "dismantled" while the new ones remain "unclear".
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Zimbabwe probes helicopter crash that killed tycoon Chivayo
item.description: Tycoon Wicknell Chivayo and his wife Lucy Muteke were among six people killed in a helicopter crash on Wednesday.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com

item.title: Algeria adopts law imposing death penalty on forest arsonists
item.description: Algerian lawmakers on Thursday voted to impose the death penalty on convicted forest arsonists, after deadly wildfires killed at least 12 people during the summer.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Amnesty accuses Morocco of spying on activists and journalists
item.description: In a new report, Amnesty International said Moroccan intelligence services use a web of surveillance to silence any critical voices.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: East African countries are racing to finish preparations ahead of AFCON 2027
item.description: With less than nine months to go before the start of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, host nations Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda are scrambling to finish preparations amid rumours of a potential relocation.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Mass funeral held in Gaza City after 105 bodies recovered from rubble
item.description: Hundreds of mourners in Gaza City held a vigil on Wednesday for 105 people killed during Israel's war on the Palestinian territory. Their bodies were recovered in the past several days, after remaining buried under the rubble for nearly three years.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Oil prices rise on stalled US-Iran talks and restrained fuel markets
item.description: Brent crude rose on Wednesday to over $100 a barrel as it recorded a monthly gain of about 14 per cent, its biggest since July.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Nigeria's president hails economic reforms ahead of bid for reelection
item.description: President Bola Tinubu lauded that the country had overcome major challenges since he assumed office in 2023 while he remains unpopular among young Nigerians with his reelection bid around the corner
item.author: editorial@africanews.com

item.title: Burkina Faso's military leaders mark four years in power
item.description: People gathered in Ougadougou’s Place de la Révolution on Wednesday night to celebrate the military government's achievements.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Ethiopia: federal forces advance in Tigray as 52 civilians reported killed
item.description: The conflict is also spreading beyond Tigray, with fighting reported in neighbouring Afar and Amhara regions. Communications remain disrupted, making independent verification of battlefield claims difficult.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com

item.title: Botswana under fire after authorising elephant killing for independence celebrations
item.description: The government of Botswana faced backlash from animal rights activists after it approved the hunting of 23 elephants to provide meat for independence celebrations.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Football: Ronaldo leaves Portugal training camp amid reported rift with coach
item.description: His departure came hours after Jorge Jesus said the forward would not start the Nations League match against Denmark on Thursday.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Thirteen sentenced to jail in France over deadly Channel migrant boat sinking
item.description: Thirteen people were sentenced to up to 10 years in prison for organising the crossing of a small boat through the English Channel in November 2021. A total of 31 migrants died when the ship sank.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Netanyahu praises passengers who helped avert disaster on Israel-bound flight
item.description: Netanyahu said he had met the Israeli passenger, whom he described as acting with extraordinary courage.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com

item.title: Mali: more than 2,400 schools remain closed as insecurity disrupts new school year
item.description: The government has made education a priority, but the security situation remains a major obstacle to reopening schools in affected areas.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com

item.title: Ethiopian Airlines signs deal to buy 10 Boeing cargo planes
item.description: State-owned company Ethiopian Airlines has agreed to buy 10 Boeing cargo aircraft, with an option to acquire eight more, in an effort to increase its cargo services.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Zimbabwe businessman Wicknell Chivayo and wife killed in helicopter crash
item.description: Police confirmed in a short statement on X that the helicopter was carrying six occupants but could not immediately confirm the identities of the victims.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com

item.title: Africa: Solid growth amid investment challenges [Business Africa]
item.description: Despite the global economic slowdown, Africa is maintaining steady growth. In the second quarter of 2026, its real GDP grew by 1.6%, compared to 0.7% for the global economy.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Yasmina El Abbasy)

item.title: DRC: Death of local official highlights tensions around Ebola response
item.description: Karondwa was buried in his native Lubero, as calls grow for an investigation into his death and for greater trust between communities and health workers fighting the Ebola outbreak.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com

item.title: Passengers of diverted flydubai flight land in Israel
item.description: Passengers on a FlyDubai flight that made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia after a violent cockpit incident, arrived in Tel Aviv on Wednesday, describing the ordeal as “very terrifying”
item.author: editorial@africanews.com

item.title: 'No backing down': S.African anti-migrant protesters vow to keep marching
item.description: South African anti-migrant protesters rallied in Durban vow to keep up their months-long fight to get undocumented migrants to leave the country
item.author: editorial@africanews.com

item.title: Tunisia president softens 'fake news' decree after criticism by rights groups
item.description: Tunisian President Kais Saied on Wednesday softened a cybercrime decree that was widely criticised by rights groups, by scrapping a five-year prison sentence for the dissemination of "fake news"
item.author: editorial@africanews.com

item.title: Three European lawmakers say humanitarian situation in Ceuta is 'grim'
item.description: Speaking following a fact-finding mission, they also accused the Spanish armed forces of 'torture' and 'inhumane treatment'.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Pix of the Day, 30 September, 2026 - Across the world
item.description: Burkina Faso has inaugurated its first gold refinery as its military-led government seeks to strengthen economic sovereignty after breaking ties with its traditional Western partners.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: FlyDubai says investigating mid-air pilot fight as Israel alleges terror plot
item.description: A pilot on a flight from the United Arab Emirates stabbed another pilot and then apparently tried to crash the aircraft carrying dozens of Israelis on Wednesday, Israel's prime minister claimed
item.author: editorial@africanews.com

item.title: IATA says African air cargo capacity rose by 14 per cent in August
item.description: The world airline body said this significantly outpaced the 3 per cent growth in cargo demand across the region.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Hundreds of South Africans protest against undocumented immigrants in Durban
item.description: Anti-migrant group March and March staged demonstrations against illegal immigration across several South African provinces on Wednesday. The movement had set the date of September 30 as a deadline for undocumented immigrants to leave the country.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: São Tomé and Príncipe's main opposition party wins most seats in polls
item.description: The Liberation Movement of São Tomé and Príncipe failed however to win an outright majority, setting the stage for talks on a coalition government.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: Rescuers pull migrants from deadly shipwreck off Tunisian Coast
item.description: At least two people, one of them a child, died and six went missing after a dramatic shipwreck off the Tunisian coast, near the Gulf of Gabes, according to the European non-profit humanitarian organisation Sea-Watch on Tuesday
item.author: editorial@africanews.com

item.title: Pope Leo XIV calls for dialogue in Ethiopia amid renewed fighting in Tigray
item.description: In his address in St. Peter's Square on Wednesday, Pope Leo XIV called on all parties involved in the latest episode of violence in northern Ethiopia to engage in dialogue.
item.author: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)
